questions.q: Why do citations matter especially in a RAG system, compared to a plain LLM answer?
options: They make the model respond faster
They let a user verify that a claim actually traces back to a specific retrieved source, rather than just trusting the model
They are required by the embedding model's API
They eliminate the need for a vector database
questions.explain: Citations turn the traceability a RAG system is supposed to have — from claim back to source — into something visible and checkable by the user.

questions.q: What is the main weakness of the manual, bracket-number citation approach?
options: It cannot be used with any vector database
It requires a completely different embedding model
It requires restructuring the entire vector database schema
It depends on the model reliably including the correct bracket number next to the correct claim, which a prompt instruction encourages but doesn't guarantee
questions.explain: Because the manual approach relies on the model following an instruction to insert bracket numbers correctly, there's no structural guarantee it always does so accurately.

questions.q: In the Messages API's built-in Citations feature, how is each retrieved chunk represented in the request?
options: As a plain string concatenated into the system prompt
As its own 'document' content block with citations enabled
As a separate API call made before the main request
As a tool_use block
questions.explain: Each chunk is sent as its own document content block with citations: {enabled: true}, which lets the API tie specific response text back to that specific document.

questions.q: What does a citation entry in the built-in Citations feature's response include?
options: Only a boolean indicating whether the answer used any document
The model's confidence score and nothing else
The exact cited_text, the document_title, and the character range it came from
A re-ranking relevance_score
questions.explain: A citation in the response includes the exact passage (cited_text), which document it came from (document_title), and the location within that document.

questions.q: What do both citation approaches depend on, regardless of which one is used?
options: The user manually tagging each answer with a source
A chunk having been stored with enough metadata at ingestion — like a source ID and page — to point back to
The re-ranker having run on every chunk
The vector database supporting hybrid search
questions.explain: Neither citation approach can point to a source that was never recorded — both depend on the metadata captured back when the chunk was ingested (Lesson 16).
